# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P35](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0035), [v2 c21 P40](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0040), [v2 c21 P43](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0043)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a little lady with snow-white hair that is thick, wavy, and arranged in becoming puffs and coils. Beneath her hair, she has an almost girlish, pink-cheeked face with dimples and big, soft, wood-brown eyes with golden glints. She wears dainty gowns, such as cream muslin patterned with pale roses, which suit her youthful charm perfectly.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

Miss Lavendar is romantic, highly imaginative, and retains an ineradicable youthfulness despite her age. She possesses a playful, imaginative mind and enjoys playing pretend games with dream-people. Although viewed by some as peculiar, she is sweet-tempered, sensible, and a warm host.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P35](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0035), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P87](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0087), [v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003), [v2 c22 P6](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0006), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)_

## Goals

- To keep her heart young and cultivate imagination despite solitude  <sub>[v2 c21 P35](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0035)</sub>

## History

Miss Lavendar Lewis grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Lewis, who named her Lavendar after his wife's favorite scent. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but after a serious quarrel twenty-five years prior, the engagement was broken off, and Stephen left for the United States. Following this, she withdrew into a secluded existence at Echo Lodge, an old stone house surrounded by woods in Grafton. During a trek through Grafton, Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her house and were welcomed to tea. The encounter led to a warm friendship, with Anne returning to visit and eventually introducing Miss Lavendar to Stephen's son, Paul Irving. Interacting with Paul helped Miss Lavendar reconnect with the past, ultimately paving the way for her eventual reunion and marriage to Stephen Irving.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P31](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0031), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P42](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0042), [v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P26](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0026), [v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he loved the scent of lavender on her mother's sheets when he first fell in love with her  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Engaged twenty-five years ago to Stephen Irving before they quarrelled and broke off their engagement  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- Lived in an isolated stone house in Grafton for years away from town life  <sub>[v2 c21 P31](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0031), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>

## Quotes

> Charlotta the Fourth says that you wished to see me  <sub>[v2 c21 P46](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0046)</sub>

> It’s very sweet, don’t you think? Mother always loved it. She planted these borders long ago. Father named me Lavendar because he was so fond of it.  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> He has blue eyes and curly hair. He steals in and wakens me with a kiss every morning. Then all day he plays here in the garden . . . and I play with him.  <sub>[v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)</sub>
